specs.scene: A documentary photograph of a small hotel front desk at eye level; a clerk stands mid-action, phone receiver lifted to one ear, the other hand resting on an open paper ledger; the counter surface is bare and unmarked; morning light comes through a nearby window; the lobby behind is visible but out of focus.
specs.source_quote: That's how the ninety percent margin claims happen, and directionally they're right

recognisable.why: A hotel front desk and clerk are instantly familiar to any viewer, though slightly less iconic than a named brand.

legibility.why: One clerk mid-action at one counter forms a single resolvable mass.

curiosity.why: The verdict asserts a margin claim is 'real' without showing proof, which a viewer would want resolved, but it is close to a flat statement rather than a sharp open loop.

subject.why: The clerk mid-action is a single clear human anchor.

credible.why: No figure is carried, which scores full by rubric.

stakes.why: Implies a viable business model for the viewer, but the connection to personal gain is inferred rather than stated.

reexpress.why: Carries a verdict distinct from the title's dollar figures, but does not sharpen those figures into a smaller honest unit.

specs.scene: A close macro shot of a single push-button telephone resting beside a small stack of blank paper slips on a hotel front-desk counter; no hands or figures are visible; the surrounding counter surface is bare and unmarked; soft directional light falls across the phone's casing.
specs.source_quote: Businesses don't buy 'automation' — they buy 'your missed calls get answered and booked.'

recognisable.why: A telephone and paper slips are universally recognisable everyday objects with no category-noun ambiguity.

legibility.why: A single object fills the frame with nothing else competing for attention.

curiosity.why: The line states an outcome rather than implying an unresolved verdict the viewer must look twice to judge.

subject.why: One distinctive object serves as a clean anchor.

credible.why: No figure is present, scoring full by rubric.

stakes.why: Implies a gain to the viewer's business (bookings recovered) but stays close to neutral description.

reexpress.why: Restates the source's mechanism language rather than converting the title's headline figure into a smaller honest unit.

specs.scene: A technician's hands adjust a small countertop card-reader device at a restaurant service counter; the technician's torso and shoulder occupy the right third of the frame, mid-action, head turned toward the device; the left half of the frame is bare countertop and wall, left open; overhead kitchen light is even and functional.
specs.source_quote: the same service, at solo scale, is a two thousand dollar project

recognisable.why: A technician at a restaurant counter is a familiar trade scene, though less iconic than a named object or brand.

legibility.why: The person and the device form two separately resolvable elements even though they share one action, costing half credit.

curiosity.why: The figure is a flat stated fact, not an unresolved verdict the viewer must puzzle over.

subject.why: A person mid-action is a clean, singular human anchor.

credible.why: The $2,000 figure matches the source's smallest honest project unit and is plausible to a sceptical operator.

stakes.why: Directly implies achievable personal income, a clear gain to the viewer.

reexpress.why: Converts the title's $5.9B/$100 framing into the smallest honest per-project unit, the textbook reexpress move.

specs.scene: A single large steel switchboard cabinet fills the frame in an industrial back room; rows of dial knobs and neatly coiled cables cover its face as unread texture; the cabinet stands alone against a bare concrete wall; overhead fluorescent light is even; no people or other objects are present.
specs.source_quote: What used to take a systems integrator and six months

recognisable.why: A switchboard cabinet is an industry-only object most cold viewers would not immediately place.

legibility.why: One machine occupies the entire frame with no competing elements.

curiosity.why: The claim of never missing a call again implies a verdict about reliability the viewer cannot confirm by looking, prompting a want to check.

subject.why: The single machine is a distinctive, unambiguous object anchor.

credible.why: No figure is carried, scoring full by rubric.

stakes.why: Implies loss avoidance (missed business) directly relevant to the viewer's own operation.

reexpress.why: Shifts from the title's dollar figures to a consequence claim, but the object itself is too industry-specific to fully carry the title's subject.
